scope: Corollary 9.1 of the manuscript “Baumslag-Solitar-free one-relator groups are hyperbolic” (preprints/Baumslag-Solitar-free-one-relator-groups-are-hyperbolic-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 258 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b578833682141115), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 50. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let X be finite, let r ∈ F(X), and suppose that G = F(X)/⟨⟨r⟩⟩ contains no subgroup isomorphic to BS(m, n) for any nonzero integers m, n. There are a finite-index subgroup H ≤ G, an integer d ≥ 0, an automorphism α of the rank-d free group Fd, and an embedding H ,→ Fd ⋊α Z. Consequently the same H fits into an exact sequence 1 −→ K −→ H −→ Q −→ 1, K free, Q ≤ Z. Thus G is virtually free-by-cyclic, with the rank of K allowed to be infinite and Q allowed to be trivial.
